questions.prompt: How is an extension method declared?
options: As an instance method in a class that inherits from the extended type
As a static method in a static class, with `this` before its first parameter
As a virtual method marked with `extends`
As a static method in any class, with `this` before its last parameter
questions.explanation: An extension method is a static method in a static class whose first parameter is prefixed with `this`; that parameter is the type being extended, so you can call it like `myObj.MyExt()`.

questions.prompt: `Person` has an instance method `Print()`, and `PersonExtensions` defines `Print(this Person p)`. Which one does `p.Print()` call?
options: The extension method, because it was declared later
Both, in declaration order
The instance method, because an instance method with the same signature wins
Neither; the call is ambiguous and doesn't compile
questions.explanation: If the type already has an instance method with the same signature, the instance method wins, so the output is `Instance Print: Aman`.

questions.prompt: Your extension method doesn't appear in IntelliSense on the type it extends. What is the likely cause?
options: The namespace containing the static class isn't imported with `using`
The extension method isn't marked `virtual`
The extended type must be `sealed`
Extension methods never appear in IntelliSense
questions.explanation: You must `using` the namespace that contains the static class for the extension method to appear in IntelliSense.

questions.prompt: How is an extension method call resolved?
options: At run time through virtual dispatch on the object's actual type
By reflection the first time the method is called
At compile time, with no virtual dispatch
By the garbage collector when the object is created
questions.explanation: Extension methods are resolved at compile time, with no virtual dispatch. You can also call one like a static method: `MyExtensions.MyMethod(obj)`.

questions.prompt: `IsValidId(this IEntity entity)` is defined in `EntityExtensions`. Which classes can call `IsValidId()`?
options: Only classes that override `IsValidId`
Only `Customer`, because it was declared first
Only classes in the same file as `EntityExtensions`
Every class that implements `IEntity`, without changing those classes
questions.explanation: Extending an interface adds the method to all classes implementing it without touching them, so `Customer` and any other `IEntity` can call `IsValidId()`.

source.section: 2. Work with Interfaces without modifying implementations
